text:
jordan_customer: Hey team — running the private/VPC installer in our prod VPC and it fails when pulling model shards and when the agent tries to send telemetry. Installer aborts with TLS errors and some DNS NXDOMAINs. Anybody seen this pattern?

alice_support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the installer log snippet (the error lines) and a quick curl/traceroute output? Also which installer version?

jordan_customer: Installer v1.9.2. Logs: 
```
2026-02-28T14:12:03Z ERROR fetcher: download failed: https://models.registry.redwood.ai/shards/abc123: TLS handshake failed: certificate verify failed: issuer not found
2026-02-28T14:12:03Z WARN telemetry: post to https://telemetry.redwood.ai/v1/ping failed: TLS alert (handshake failure)
2026-02-28T14:12:04Z ERROR resolver: lookup models.registry.redwood.ai: no such host
```

Also tried: `curl -v https://models.registry.redwood.ai/health` gives `curl: (6) Could not resolve host: models.registry.redwood.ai` from the host running the installer, but from my laptop DNS resolves fine.

maria_sre: Sounds like split-horizon DNS or a proxy intercepting TLS. Can you run these from the host running the installer and paste outputs?
1) `dig +short models.registry.redwood.ai`
2) `openssl s_client -connect models.registry.redwood.ai:443 -servername models.registry.redwood.ai`
3) `curl -v --resolve models.registry.redwood.ai:443:3.4.5.6 https://models.registry.redwood.ai/health` (replace IP from dig)

jordan_customer: Outputs: 
1) `dig +short models.registry.redwood.ai` -> (no output)
2) `openssl s_client -connect 3.4.5.6:443 -servername models.registry.redwood.ai` -> returns a cert for `intercept.local` and `verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate`
3) `curl --resolve` returns same cert name mismatch.

alice_support: That confirms DNS or a proxy in path returning internal intercept cert; installer and runtime require SNI passthrough (we use SNI to route to multi-tenant frontends and the cert must present the upstream SAN). If your gateway terminates TLS (corporate TLS inspect), it will break signature validation for our shards and telemetry. Two short options: 1) allow TLS passthrough for our hosts (recommended), or 2) add our CA used by your proxy to the host CA bundle (less ideal).

maria_sre: To unblock quickly, here's a minimal egress allowlist we've used with other customers (hosts + ports + notes). Please ask your network team to permit outbound TLS passthrough on 443 to these FQDNs (SNI must be preserved):
- models.registry.redwood.ai (443) — model metadata & shard negotiation; DNS must resolve to public IPs
- shard-*.storage.redwood-inference.net (443) — model shard servers (wildcard)
- auth.redwood.ai (443) — token exchange and licensing
- telemetry.redwood.ai (443) — anonymized telemetry pings and installer heartbeats
- packages.redwood.ai, files.pythonhosted.org, pypi.org (443) — pip deps during install
- registry.npmjs.org (443) — npm deps if using node helper (optional)
- ocsp.int-x.example (ports 80/443) and crl distribution points used by your TLS stack — ensure OCSP stapling/OCSP requests can reach CA endpoints (some TLS stacks call back to CA servers)
- S3 endpoints used for prefetch (e.g., storage.googleapis.com or s3.amazonaws.com) if you mirror model shards

Also allow DNS (UDP 53) to a resolver that can reach the public records for these names or configure split-horizon appropriately. If you have a private resolver that intentionally NXDOMAINs unknown hosts, add exceptions or forwarders for the above domains.

alice_support: If your network MUST intercept TLS and you can't enable passthrough, two mitigations we recommend: 1) add the intercepting CA to the OS/container trust store on every host running the installer/agent, and 2) whitelist SNI and ALPN values for our hosts so the interceptor can route without re-signing critical backend certs. Note: adding CA is a security decision and not our recommended default.

jordan_customer: Quick question — which exact IP ranges should we open? Our firewall team wants CIDRs, not just hostnames.

maria_sre: We publish a short list for quick firewall policies (these are for control plane endpoints; shard storage uses cloud provider IPs that can change — prefer FQDN allowlist or use an egress proxy that respects SNI). Current control-plane IPs (small set):
- 3.4.5.6/32 (models.registry.redwood.ai)
- 3.4.5.7/32 (auth.redwood.ai)
- 3.4.5.8/32 (telemetry.redwood.ai)

Important: model shard storage uses large provider ranges (e.g., Google Cloud / AWS). Please allow outbound to `storage.googleapis.com` and `s3.amazonaws.com` by FQDN or allow the cloud provider ranges for your region. If your firewall cannot do FQDN rules, request a specific CIDR list from your vendor and keep it updated.

alice_support: Repro steps we asked for so support can validate after changes:
1) From a host in the failing subnet: `dig +short models.registry.redwood.ai` -> should return IPv4/IPv6 public address, not empty.
2) `curl -v https://models.registry.redwood.ai/health` -> HTTP 200 and JSON `{"status":"ok"}` (we return 200 for health endpoint).
3) `openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -servername models.registry.redwood.ai -showcerts` -> cert CN or SAN must include `models.registry.redwood.ai`.
4) Re-run installer with `--debug` and capture `/var/log/redwood-installer.log` and attach.

jordan_customer: Network team confirmed their TLS proxy was re-signing certs and returning `intercept.local`. They've added an allow rule for models.registry.redwood.ai and turned on passthrough for `*.redwood.ai` for the installer subnet. Will test now.

deploy-bot: deploy 1952 started by jordan_customer at 2026-02-28T15:01:10Z

jordan_customer: After the firewall change: `dig +short models.registry.redwood.ai` -> `3.4.5.6` and `curl -v https://models.registry.redwood.ai/health` -> `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` with body `{"status":"ok"}`. Installer resumed and completed model pull. Telemetry post now returns 202. Thanks! :raised_hands:

alice_support: Great — one follow-up for long-term ops: configure your egress proxy or firewall to allow SNI passthrough for our domains and prefer FQDN rules for shard storage. We can provide a script to detect TLS re-signing across the fleet if you want.

maria_sre: Also watch for intermittent failures when your NAT IPs change — consider tagging and reserving fixed egress IPs if you want to lock to CIDRs. If you need an up-to-date JSON of our control-plane IPs for firewall automation, ping us and we'll generate it for your account.

jordan_customer: Will do — please send the JSON. Thanks for the quick turnaround.

alice_support: Sending the JSON to your account contact and closing this thread, reopen if anything pops up. :white_check_mark:
